questiontext.text:
A particle moves along a straight line with displacement \(s = {@s@}\) metres after \(t\) seconds. For each time, describe the motion.

At \(t = {@exd(t1)@}\) s: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
At \(t = {@exd(t2)@}\) s: [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
At \(t = {@exd(t3)@}\) s: [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
The sign of \(v\) gives the direction of motion. The particle is speeding up when \(v\) and \(a\) have the same sign (pulling the same way), and slowing down when their signs differ.

\(v = \dfrac{ds}{dt} = {@v@}\) and \(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = {@a@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Differentiation II: speeding up or slowing down

Grade 12 CBE Core 4.1: Describe the direction of motion of a particle and whether it is speeding up or slowing down at three times, from the signs of v and a.

Core

This question is original to this project.
